title: Vegas Winners Review 2026: Pricing, Record, Is It Worth It?
description: Vegas Winners review, checked 20 Nov 2026: Wayne Allyn Root's pick store, $30 picks, no refunds, no full record, a parent with $594 of revenue, buyer posts.
dek: VegasWinners.com is the pick store built around Wayne Allyn Root. On 20 Nov 2026 it had one fresh pick for sale, Root's, at $30. The refund policy says no refunds, the site publishes no full pick log, and its parent company told the SEC in October 2026 that it earned $594 in the first half of 2026 and is now focused on a prediction market product.

status.label: Not verified
status.note: Watchdog has not graded a full, time stamped record for Vegas Winners or any of its handicappers. This page reports what we could check on 20 Nov 2026 and labels everything else.

short_answer: Vegas Winners is a real business with a named operator, a Las Vegas mailing address, a phone number, a New Jersey gaming vendor registration and a parent company that files with the SEC. It is still taking orders: on 20 Nov 2026 it listed one Wayne Allyn Root college football pick for that night at $30.

It is a thin and fading store, though. The only other picks listed for sale were dated December 2023 and February 2024, one handicapper profile still leads with plays from a January 2022 playoff game, and a homepage notice says the company is "PREPARING TO TRANSITION FROM WEB SALES TO A PERSONAL VIP EMAIL" service. The parent company's October 2026 SEC filing reports $594 of revenue for the first half of 2026 and describes its core product as a prediction market platform, not pick sales.

There is no full pick log, no refund and no outside monitor we could find. Buyer talk over almost 20 years is sparse and mostly skeptical of Root's record. If you buy, buy one pick at a time and keep your own log.
pricing_intro: Prices below were shown on VegasWinners.com on 20 Nov 2026. The site has a Shop Subscriptions menu item but showed no subscription prices; month and season deals are offered by email.
pricing: $30. One pick listed for 20 Nov 2026 ("CFB GREAT MATCHUP TONIGHT")
No refund. Credit only "in specific individual cases"
$30 each. The two listed were dated 19 Dec 2023 and 13 Feb 2024
Month or season VIP email service
Not shown. The homepage says "IF YOU BUY ONE GAME A DAY FOR 30 DAYS, THAT'S $900. THIS IS SO MUCH LESS" and asks buyers to email for a "MONTH OR SEASON SPECIAL"
No coupon codes were shown on 20 Nov 2026. On 17 Nov the site advertised "Free $1000 of Coupons for Premium Picks" and "Every 4th Item in Your Cart is FREE!"
guarantee: The refund policy is one line: "No refunds, but credit applied in specific individual cases." It does not say which cases.

The terms of service say "there are no guaranteed winners and VegasWinners.com does not guarantee a winner from any picks sold," and the site and services are provided "AS IS" and "AS AVAILABLE." The terms say Florida law governs and that the site is "created and controlled by VegasWinners.com Inc. in the State of Florida," although the address is in Nevada. Buyers must be 21 or older. We saw no guarantee offered on any pick, so every loss, on both the pick price and the bet, falls on the buyer.

claims_note: How we checked: we divided wins by wins plus losses for every record that gave both numbers. Most of the math holds, but several figures are rounded up (18 and 8 shown as 70% is really 69.2%), one does not add up at all (8 and 3 from "LAST 7" plays), and one counts 147 plays as 146. None comes with a date range or a list of the plays behind it, and most are from 2017 to 2020.

The sales copy is out of date. "37 Years of Winners" counted from 1985 was true around 2022; in 2026 it would be 41. Ross Benjamin's profile still leads with a 49ers and Rams NFC Championship play, a game played in January 2022, and two Chip Chirimbes picks from 2023 and 2024 are still listed for sale at $30. The same 20 Nov listing that sells Root's pick says he went 0 and 2 the day before with "a bad choice in the NFL with Indy."

Root himself has been open about the sales side. In a 2004 Daily Racing Form article on an ESPN series about touts, he said "I'm an entertainer and a salesman," and described how a seller could present a good week as a high winning percentage while leaving out a bad one. That is a fair warning to apply to any streak on this site.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: nothing we could find. We found no full, time stamped pick log, no monitoring service result we could open and no contest result for Vegas Winners as a store.
What Vegas Winners publishes: streak lines on each profile and a sales blurb on each pick. There is no archive of past picks with results that we could find.

A 2021 press release from the parent company said Root's picks were "independently monitored and documented" but did not name the monitor. Forum members as far back as 2007 said Root's record could not be checked because it was not monitored. Root's plays are still reposted on TheSpread forum, for example 19 bowl and NFL plays from 23 Dec 2025 to 4 Jan 2026, but nobody there posted results, so even that is not a record.

The business behind it: the parent, Winners, Inc., filed a Regulation A offering in 2026. Its 22 Oct 2026 amendment says it had $594 of revenue and a net loss of $133,275 in the six months to 30 Jun 2026, $24,600 of cash, a working capital deficit of $550,616, and substantial doubt about its ability to continue. For 2025 it reported a net loss of $886,322 and $165 of cash at year end. It says Winners had "insignificant operations" when it merged with Moneyline Sports in September 2025, that its CEO is now a part time executive who also runs a finance firm, and that its core product is Mevu.com, a prediction market platform working with Kalshi and Polymarket. Root signed a three year CEO contract in July 2023 at $10,000 a month; the current filing lists a different CEO.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no Vegas Winners handicapper is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how these handicappers perform.
our_data.context: For scale: Vegas Winners copy cites runs of 68% to 75%. On the Watchdog board, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Buyer evidence on Vegas Winners as a store is very thin. CapperTek lists it with no reviews and the Better Business Bureau has no listing. The main material is a 2023 TheRX thread where subscribers discussed Root's plays, a 2025 TheSpread comment, and older forum talk about Root himself from before Vegas Winners existed. Our Reddit search was partial: the Reddit archive's full text search timed out or refused requests on 17 and 20 Nov 2026, and our saved copy of r/sportsbook and r/sportsbetting posts from 2024 to 2026 had no mention of Vegas Winners.

customers.text: We found five independent threads that matter, spread over almost 20 years and three forums, plus forum rules and reposts. In January 2023 two TheRX members who said they paid for a Root subscription shared his plays; others argued over whether the posted plays were real, one said Root was slow to update his site, and another said the money was better spent elsewhere. In October 2025 a TheSpread member called Root the worst of the services that release picks days ahead. A Sportsbook Review thread from 2007 and 2008 was hostile to Root's marketing and unmonitored record. TheRX has listed Root among services members should not post since at least 2023. Nobody posted a tracked result, and we found no positive buyer review and no review site entries. The pattern is thin but one sided: skepticism of the record, little talk of the store itself.

Two members said they held paid Root subscriptions, one a yearly one, and received his plays by email, sometimes with extra plays not shown on the website. Others said VegasWinners listed only one play that day, and the exchange turned into an argument about which list was correct.

In the same thread, one member said Root's picks are not worth following and that the subscription money would be better spent on services with higher win rates. Another said Root is slow to update his site, and a third asked why a service would hold back its biggest plays instead of selling them.

On TheSpread, when a member asked whether anyone received Root's selections, the thread starter said they do not follow services that release picks five or six days before games, and called Root the worst offender among them.
TheSpread members reposted Root's rated plays through bowl season and the end of the NFL regular season, such as "Millionaire", "Pinnacle" and "Gold Standard" plays. Nobody posted how they did.
TheRX service play guidelines list Wayne Root under "Do not post these services." The rules give no reason, and many sellers are on the same list.

Before Vegas Winners existed, Sportsbook Review members questioned ads claiming 80% winners on Root's locks. They said his reputation rested on one strong NFL season in the late 1980s, that he declined to have his record monitored, and one recalled him going 1 and 6 in a 1990s celebrity contest. These are old, unverified forum claims about Root, not about the current store.

CapperTek lists VegasWinners.com with "no reviews or complaints." A Better Business Bureau search for vegas winners returned no matching business. Web searches found no complaint or regulator action under the Vegas Winners name. We did not read Trustpilot.

conflicts: The main handicapper is also the face and a former chief executive of the business. The SEC filing says Root signed a three year agreement in July 2023 to serve as CEO of Winners, Inc. at $10,000 a month; since September 2025 the filing lists another person as CEO. The About page still calls Root CEO. Root's picks, his records and the company's sales are tied together.

VegasWinners registered as a sports betting affiliate, which a 2021 release says earns either a flat fee per new depositing customer or a share of revenue from bettors it refers to sportsbooks. We did not see current affiliate links or terms, but an affiliate earns more when its readers bet more.

The site carries an Investors section with press releases, SEC filings and a stock quote. Upbeat pick records have also appeared in the company's stock market press releases, so the same claims serve both buyers and investors.
The parent's new core product is a prediction market platform working with Kalshi and Polymarket. Pick sales now appear to be a side line of a company with other priorities.
strengths: Named operator, Las Vegas mailing address and a customer service phone number.
Single picks at a flat $30, with no long contract needed.
A parent company that files public reports with the SEC, so its finances can be read.
A New Jersey gaming vendor registration that was active on 19 Nov 2026.
The listing is honest about recent losses, such as the 0 and 2 day shown next to the 20 Nov pick.
concerns: No full pick log; only undated or years old streaks, some rounded up and one that does not add up.
Only one handicapper had a current pick for sale; other listings and profiles are years out of date.
The parent company reported $594 of revenue and $24,600 of cash for the first half of 2026, substantial doubt about continuing, and a new core business in prediction markets.
A planned move to email only VIP sales with prices not shown, which would remove even the current public listings.
Buyer talk we found was mostly skeptical, and none of it was a tracked record.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, odds and send time. A streak with no start date is not a record.
Before you prepay for a month or season by email, get the price, the start and end dates and the refund terms in writing.
Ask which "specific individual cases" earn a credit before you buy.
Count units, not wins. A 70% run over a few weeks means little.
Read the parent company's latest SEC filing; a seller in financial trouble may not be around to deliver a season package.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner.
faq: It is a real company, Vegas Winners Inc., with a Las Vegas address, a phone number and a New Jersey vendor registration, and it still sells Wayne Allyn Root picks at $30 each. We could not verify that its picks win over time: there is no full public record, and the refund policy offers no refunds.
How much does Vegas Winners cost?
On 20 Nov 2026 each pick cost $30. Month and season deals were not priced on the site; the homepage asked buyers to email for a VIP deal and compared it with $900 for one pick a day for 30 days.

The terms name Vegas Winners Inc. SEC filings by Winners, Inc. of Reno, NV say it acquired about 97% of VegasWinners, Inc. in 2020. Root signed on as CEO of Winners, Inc. in July 2023; since a September 2025 merger with Moneyline Sports the filings list a different, part time CEO.
No. The policy says "No refunds, but credit applied in specific individual cases," without saying which cases, and the terms say there are no guaranteed winners.

It says it is licensed by state gaming regulators. We found Vegas Winners Inc on New Jersey's active gaming vendor list dated 19 Nov 2026, and 2021 releases describe registrations as a sports betting affiliate, which allows it to earn commissions for referring bettors. A vendor registration is not a check on pick results.

Nothing we found shows it is. The records are undated or old streaks, there are no refunds, much of the store looks unmaintained, and the parent company reports almost no revenue and substantial doubt about continuing. If you try it, buy one pick at a time and keep your own log.
